title: Workflow Record
description: One surveyed microbial ecology analysis composition. The record is a chain of steps captured twice — as claimed by the paper's Methods, and as observed in the attached code — plus the divergence between them, an applicability block for matching against new datasets, and a two-stage vetting result.

id.description: Stable slug, also the catalog filename. Convention: firstauthor-year-keyword, or org-name for registry workflows (e.g. 'nf-core-mag').

name.description: Human-readable name of the workflow as the authors call it.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what this composition does, for what data.

archetype.description: One or more archetypes from schema/ontology/archetypes.yaml. Multiple when a paper runs e.g. amplicon and metagenome arms.

provenance.description: Where this record came from. At least one of `sources` or `code` must be non-empty.

sources.description: Literature records. A single work appearing as preprint and journal article gets one entry per venue.

id.description: arXiv ID, bioRxiv DOI, PMID, PMCID, DOI, or registry slug.

license.description: Article license, e.g. cc-by. Governs whether we may cache full text.

fulltext_available.description: Whether Methods text was retrievable. False means `claimed` was extracted from abstract only.

code.description: Attached implementations. Empty array is meaningful — it is the primary reproducibility signal.

resolves.description: Did the URL actually return a repository at ingest time.

commit.description: SHA or tag pinned at extraction time. Everything in `observed` refers to this snapshot.

entrypoints.description: Repo-relative paths that define the chain (main.nf, Snakefile, *.cwl, run.sh, analysis.Rmd).

claimed.description: The composition as described in the paper's Methods section. Extracted from text; every step should carry evidence pointing at the sentence it came from.

observed.description: The composition as it exists in code, read from the pinned commit. Null when no code is attached — not an empty chain, which would mean 'code exists and does nothing'.

divergence.description: Diff between claimed and observed. Empty array only means agreement if `observed` is non-null; when observed is null this must be empty and carries no information.

role.description: Which step role the divergence sits at, when it maps to one.

applicability.description: What data this workflow is valid for. The matching surface. Keys mirror SRA/ENA vocabulary so dataset metadata joins directly; an omitted or empty array means 'unconstrained on this axis', which matches everything.

depth_min_reads.description: Per-sample floor below which the authors' chain is not expected to work.

environment.description: Sample environments demonstrated in the source. Advisory for ranking, not a hard filter — a soil chain usually runs fine on sediment.

requires_multiple_samples.description: True for chains with co-assembly, differential abundance, or cross-sample binning steps.

requires_replication.description: True when downstream statistics assume biological replicates.

reference_databases.description: External DBs the chain cannot run without. Size drives whether an agent can realistically stage this.

name.description: e.g. SILVA, GTDB, UNITE, CheckM2, Kraken2 standard, KEGG, Pfam.

version.description: Null/absent here is what raises a db_unspecified divergence.

licensed.description: True for DBs needing a paid or registered license (e.g. KEGG).

excluded.description: Explicit anti-matches the authors or adjudicator called out, e.g. 'not valid for single-end amplicon data'.

outputs.description: Terminal artifacts the chain produces. Lets an agent match on desired result, not just input data.

runnability.description: Can an agent actually execute this. Objective, recomputed on re-ingest.

source.description: Where the numbers came from. 'estimated' means the adjudicator guessed and they are soft.

hpc_ready.description: Chain declares an executor/profile suitable for SLURM-style batch submission.

tier.description: reference = runnable, pinned, tested, judged sound. usable = runnable with work. documented = chain is legible but code isn't runnable. paper_only = no code. rejected = failed adjudication or superseded by a strictly better record.

scorecard.description: Stage 1: objective signals, stored verbatim so weighting can change without re-ingest. Do not store a single composite score here — compute it at query time.

adjudication.description: Stage 2: LLM judgment. A re-derivable artifact, never ground truth — always overridden by human_review.

model.description: Exact model ID that produced this judgment.

prompt_version.description: Version of the adjudication prompt in extract/prompts/.

chain_matches_claims.description: Does the composition do what the abstract/title says it does.

soundness_notes.description: Methodological concerns, e.g. 'rarefies before ANCOM-BC', 'no negative controls in a low-biomass system'.

caveats.description: Practical warnings for anyone reusing this chain.

human_review.description: Always wins over adjudication. Presence of `tier_override` pins the record's tier.

roleId.description: A step role from schema/ontology/step_roles.yaml. Validated against that file by scripts/validate.py, not by JSON Schema.

toolId.description: A canonical tool ID from schema/ontology/tools.yaml. Unknown tools are allowed but flagged by the validator so the ontology can grow.

chain.description: An ordered DAG of steps. `steps` carries the nodes; edges are implicit in `order` for linear chains and explicit via `depends_on` when the graph branches.

source.description: How this chain was derived. `abstract_only` marks a low-fidelity claimed chain.

extracted_from.description: Locators — section names for text, repo-relative file paths for code.

completeness.description: sketch = tools named but order uncertain.

step_id.description: Local ID, required only if other steps reference it via depends_on.

order.description: Topological position. Steps sharing an order run in parallel / are alternatives — disambiguate with `alternative_of`.

depends_on.description: step_ids this consumes output from. Omit for a linear chain.

tool_raw.description: Verbatim name as written in the paper or invoked in the code, before normalization. Kept for auditability.

optional.description: Step is conditional/flag-gated in the code, or described as optional in the text.

alternative_of.description: step_id this is an either/or alternative to, e.g. MEGAHIT vs metaSPAdes behind one config flag.

params.description: Notable non-default parameters only. Free-form key/value — the point is to capture choices that change results (trunc_len, min_contig_len, --meta), not to reproduce the full CLI.

database.description: Reference DB this step consumes, e.g. 'SILVA 138.1'.

purpose.description: One short clause on why this step is here, when it isn't obvious from the role.

evidence.description: Pointer back to the exact text or code this assertion came from. Required discipline: no extracted claim without a locator.

locator.description: Section name ('Methods > Sequence processing') or repo-relative path with line range ('workflows/assembly.nf#L40-L58').

quote.description: Verbatim snippet. Keep short; respect the source license recorded in provenance.
